source.howDecided: git log 3cf2963cd0..origin/main over all six culprit files (create-envelope-recipients.ts, assert-envelope-mutable.ts, update-envelope-recipients.ts, delete-envelope-recipient.ts, create-envelope-fields.ts, update-envelope-fields.ts) returns zero commits. Stronger check: git rev-parse on each blob at both revisions returns the SAME sha for all six, so the files are byte-identical between v2.16.0 and v2.17.0 and line numbers have not drifted. Read the culprit region at origin/main: line 68 is still `assertEnvelopeMutable(envelope);`, lines 70-74 are still `if (envelope.completedAt) { throw new AppError(AppErrorCode.INVALID_REQUEST, { message: 'Envelope already complete' }); }`, and line 100 is still the transaction-scoped `await assertEnvelopeMutable(envelope, tx);`. There is still no comparison of envelope.status to DocumentStatus.DRAFT anywhere on the path. Read assert-envelope-mutable.ts at origin/main: assertSnapshotMutable still opens with `if (!isTspEnvelope(envelope)) { return; }` at lines 65-67, so it is still inert for the default SES envelope. The bound doc sentence also survives: origin/main:apps/docs/content/docs/developers/api/documents.mdx still reads 'You cannot modify recipients or fields after a document moves to `PENDING` status.', now at line 898 (it was line 755 at v2.16.0; the file grew via #3022 'chore: deprecate endpoints' and #3135 'docs(api): document cancel endpoint and fix get-many body shape'). apps/docs/content/docs/concepts/document-lifecycle.mdx and apps/docs/content/docs/users/documents/add-recipients.mdx are byte-identical to the tested revision, so all three promises still stand.

newItems.title: setDocumentRecipients and setFieldsForDocument delete already-signed recipients and fields
newItems.note: Filed 2026-08-13, after the review's search date but before the review was written; the review does not cite it. Same family (authoring mutations on a document that has already moved past DRAFT) but a different code path: the v1 set-* replace endpoints destroying existing rows, not the v2 create-many accepting a new one on PENDING. A filer should cross-reference it, not treat it as a duplicate.

newItems.title: Adding a recipient through API v1 recreates all the others: signing links die and fields are lost
newItems.note: Closest new neighbour: also about adding a recipient to an existing document over the API. Different endpoint (v1 setDocumentRecipients) and different harm (collateral recreation of the other recipients). It does NOT report that a PENDING document accepts the addition at all, which is this finding. Not a duplicate.

reevaluation: The finding stands, unchanged and unweakened. Every one of the six culprit files is byte-identical between the tested v2.16.0 and today's v2.17.0, so the defect ships in the newest release exactly as reviewed: createEnvelopeRecipients gates only on assertEnvelopeMutable (a no-op for SES) plus envelope.completedAt, and update-envelope-recipients, delete-envelope-recipient, create-envelope-fields and update-envelope-fields carry the same two-gate shape. All three doc pages that promise the freeze are still live, one of them having merely moved line (documents.mdx:755 to :898). The review's fixedAfter claim ('still broken on main') is still correct; its only detail that has aged is the head sha it cites (688ef2fd, 2026-08-14) and the documents.mdx line number. Nothing in the 135 issues and PRs opened between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-19 reports this: the two nearest, #3188 and #3189, are both v1 set-* endpoints and both are about collateral destruction of existing rows rather than the missing PENDING guard. Scope note for the filer: steps 8-12 of the scenario, the recipient update, recipient delete and field write refusals, still have no runtime evidence and are source-level inference only, so the issue body should either present them as 'the same two-gate shape, so we expect the same result' or be backed by the live re-run the plan schedules.
policyBasis: SECURITY.md: 'Report security vulnerabilities privately. Do not open a public issue, discussion, or pull request for security reports.' plus 'If you're unsure whether something is in scope, report it privately anyway and we'll happily take a look.' The scope exclusions (SSRF, DNS, rate limiting, TLS/headers, self-hosted misconfiguration) do not cover it: this is application authorization logic in the repo's own code, which SECURITY.md's Scope section explicitly does cover.
notes: The security routing is a judgement call, not a slam dunk, and the filer should decide deliberately. Arguments for the advisory form: it is an unenforced authorization rule on a first-party API that lets a token holder add a signing party to a document other parties already agreed to sign, which lands on the signing certificate; SECURITY.md tells you to report privately when unsure. Arguments for a public issue: the actor is an authenticated same-team API-token holder acting inside their own tenant, so it is a missing business rule rather than a privilege escalation, and the maintainers evidently take comparable integrity bugs publicly (#3188, #3189, #2475 'Ghost Recipients'). If the advisory route is chosen and the maintainers say it is out of scope, refile it as a public bug report; do not file both at once. Also note documenso runs OpenAI Codex security analysis over the codebase and warns it may close a report as a duplicate of a Codex finding. One legitimate exception the fix must preserve, already recorded in the review and worth repeating in the report: documentMeta.allowDictateNextSigner lets a signer nominate the next recipient on a PENDING envelope.
